495:
Fifth Sutta.

## 6. Saṃsappanīya Sutta

216. "Monks, I will teach you the Dhamma exposition on creeping. Listen and pay close attention to it; I will speak." "Yes, Bhante," those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

Monks, what is the Dhamma exposition on creeping? Monks, beings are the owners of their kamma, heirs of their kamma, born of their kamma, related to their kamma, and have kamma as their refuge. Whatever kamma they do—whether good or evil—they are the heirs to that.

Monks, here in this world, a certain person is a killer of living beings; he is cruel, bloody-handed, given to striking and killing, and merciless to all living beings. He creeps by body, he creeps by speech, he creeps by mind. His bodily action is crooked, his verbal action is crooked, his mental action is crooked, his destination (gati) is crooked, and his rebirth (upapatti) is crooked.

Monks, for one whose destination is crooked and whose rebirth is crooked, I say there is one of two destinations: either the hell of absolute suffering or the animal realm of those that creep. And what, monks, is the animal realm of those that creep? Snakes, scorpions, centipedes, mongooses, cats, mice, owls, or whatever other animals creep upon seeing humans. Thus, monks, the rebirth of a being comes about through the being [itself]. One is reborn through what one does. When one has been reborn, contacts touch him. Thus, monks, I say that beings are the heirs of their kamma.

Monks, here in this world, a certain person takes what is not given... [p]... engages in sexual misconduct... tells lies... speaks malicious words... speaks harsh words... engages in frivolous chatter... is covetous... has a mind of ill will... has wrong view and distorted vision, [thinking]: 'There is no merit in giving... [p]... there are no ascetics and brahmins in the world who have reached the right path, who practice rightly, and who, having realized for themselves by direct knowledge, proclaim this world and the next.' He creeps by body, he creeps by speech, he creeps by mind. His bodily action is crooked, his verbal action is crooked, his mental action is crooked, his destination (gati) is crooked, and his rebirth is crooked. Monks, for one whose destination is crooked and whose rebirth is crooked, I say there is one of two destinations: either the hell of absolute suffering or the animal realm of those that creep. And what, monks, is the animal realm of those that creep?
496:
Snakes, scorpions, centipedes, mongooses, cats, mice, owls, or whatever other animals creep upon seeing humans. Thus, monks, the rebirth of a being comes about through the being [itself]. One is reborn through what one does. When one has been reborn, contacts touch him. Thus, monks, I say that beings are the heirs of their kamma. Monks, beings are the owners of their kamma, heirs of their kamma, born of their kamma, related to their kamma, and have kamma as their refuge. Whatever kamma they do—whether good or evil—they are the heirs to that.

Monks, here in this world, a certain person, having abandoned the destruction of life, abstains from the destruction of life. He has laid aside the rod, has laid aside the sword; he is conscientious, merciful, and dwells compassionate for the welfare of all living beings. He does not creep by body, he does not creep by speech, he does not creep by mind. His bodily action is straight, his verbal action is straight, his mental action is straight, his destination (gati) is straight, and his rebirth is straight.

Monks, for one whose destination is straight and whose rebirth is straight, I say there is one of two destinations: either the heavens of absolute happiness or those high-class families such as wealthy Khattiya families, wealthy Brāhmaṇa families, or wealthy Gahapati families, who are rich, with great wealth and great possessions, with abundant gold and silver, abundant assets and means, and abundant money and grain. Thus, monks, the rebirth of a being comes about through the being [itself]. One is reborn through what one does. When one has been reborn, contacts touch him. Thus, monks, I say that beings are the heirs of their kamma.

Monks, here in this world, a certain person, having abandoned taking what is not given, abstains from taking what is not given... [p]... abstains from sexual misconduct... having abandoned false speech, abstains from false speech... having abandoned malicious speech, abstains from malicious speech... having abandoned harsh speech, abstains from harsh speech... having abandoned frivolous chatter, abstains from frivolous chatter.

He is not covetous and has a mind free from ill will. He has right view and an undistorted vision, [thinking]: 'There is merit in giving... [p]... there are ascetics and brahmins in the world who have reached the right path, who practice rightly, and who, having realized for themselves by direct knowledge, proclaim this world and the next.' He does not creep by body, he does not creep by speech, he does not creep by mind. His bodily action is straight, his verbal action is straight, his mental action is straight, his destination (gati) is straight,
497:
The occurrence (in life) is straight. Monks, for one whose destination (gati) is straight and whose occurrence (in life) is straight, I declare one of two destinations: either the heavens which are exclusively pleasant, or those high-class families such as wealthy khattiya families, wealthy brāhmaṇa families, or wealthy householder families—rich, with great wealth and property, abundant gold and silver, abundant assets and means, and abundant money and grain. Thus, monks, due to the existence (of kamma), the rebirth of a being occurs. One is reborn according to the kamma one performs. When reborn, the (nature of) contacts touch him. Thus, monks, I say that 'beings are heirs to their kamma.' Monks, beings are owners of their kamma, heirs to their kamma, born of their kamma, related to their kamma, and have kamma as their refuge. Whatever kamma they do—whether good or evil—to that they will be the heirs. Monks, this is the exposition of the Dhamma on the way of trembling.

Sixth Sutta.

## 7. Paṭhamasañcetanikasutta

217. Monks, I do not say that there is an ending of volitional kamma that has been performed, instigated, and accumulated without having experienced its results. And that result is experienced either in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent life. Monks, I do not say that there is a making an end of suffering without having experienced the results of volitional kamma that has been performed, instigated, and accumulated.

In this regard, monks, there are three types of failure and corruption of bodily action, which are unwholesome and volitional, resulting in suffering and yielding suffering. There are four types of failure and corruption of verbal action, which are unwholesome and volitional, resulting in suffering and yielding suffering. There are three types of failure and corruption of mental action, which are unwholesome and volitional, resulting in suffering and yielding suffering. Monks, how are there three types of failure and corruption of bodily action which are unwholesome and volitional, resulting in suffering and yielding suffering? Here, monks, someone is a killer of living beings; he is cruel, bloody-handed, given to killing and striking, and merciless to all living beings.

He is a taker of what is not given; he takes with the intention of stealing the wealth and property of others, whether in the village or in the forest, that has not been given to him. He is a practitioner of sexual misconduct; he has sexual relations with such women as are protected by their mother... [pe]... even those adorned with a flower garland.
498: Monks, thus there are three types of failure and corruption of bodily action, which are unwholesome and volitional, resulting in suffering and yielding suffering. Monks, how are there four types of failure and corruption of verbal action which are unwholesome and volitional, resulting in suffering and yielding suffering? Here, monks, someone is a speaker of falsehood. When he is in a council, in an assembly, among relatives, among a guild, or in the royal court, and is summoned as a witness and questioned: 'Come, good man, tell what you know,' not knowing, he says, 'I know,' or knowing, he says, 'I do not know'; not seeing, he says, 'I see,' or seeing, he says, 'I do not see.' Thus, for his own sake, or for the sake of another, or for the sake of some material gain, he consciously speaks falsehood. He is a speaker of divisive speech. Having heard something here, he repeats it there to divide these people; or having heard something there, he repeats it here to divide those people. Thus, he is a divider of those who are united, an encourager of those who are divided, one who delights in factions (vagga), loves factions, rejoices in factions, and speaks words that create factions. He is a speaker of harsh speech. He speaks such words as are offensive, rough, bitter to others, abusive to others, bordering on anger, and not conducive to concentration. He is a speaker of idle chatter. He speaks at the wrong time, speaks what is not a fact, speaks what is useless, speaks what is not the Dhamma, speaks what is not the Vinaya. He speaks words that are not worth treasuring, at the wrong time, without reason, without limit, and not connected with the goal. Monks, thus there are four types of failure and corruption of verbal action, which are unwholesome and volitional, resulting in suffering and yielding suffering. Monks, how are there three types of failure and corruption of mental action which are unwholesome and volitional, resulting in suffering and yielding suffering? Here, monks, someone is covetous. He covets the wealth and property of others, thinking: 'Oh, may what belongs to another be mine!' He has a mind of ill will; he has a mind of destructive intent, thinking: 'May these beings be killed, slaughtered, cut off, destroyed, or may they not exist!' He has wrong view: 'There is no [result in] giving... [pe]... neither this world...'
499:
...nor are there in the world any ascetics and brahmins who have attained the right path and practiced rightly, and who, having realized this world and the next by their own direct knowledge, make them known.' He has such a distorted view. Thus, bhikkhus, the three types of failure in mental action are unwholesome volitional activity, resulting in suffering and yielding the fruit of suffering.

Bhikkhus, because of the three types of failure in bodily action, which are unwholesome volitional activity, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower world, in hell. 

Bhikkhus, because of the four types of failure in verbal action, which are unwholesome volitional activity, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower world, in hell. Bhikkhus, because of the three types of failure in mental action, which are unwholesome volitional activity, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower world, in hell.

Bhikkhus, just as a four-sided die, when thrown upwards, rests firmly on whichever side it lands; even so, bhikkhus, because of the three types of failure in bodily action, which are unwholesome volitional activity, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower world, in hell. Because of the four types of failure in verbal action, which are unwholesome volitional activity, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower world, in hell. Because of the three types of failure in mental action, which are unwholesome volitional activity, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower world, in hell.

Bhikkhus, I do not say that there is an ending of volitional kamma that has been done and accumulated without having experienced its results, and that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent life. Bhikkhus, I do not say that there is an ending of suffering without having experienced the results of volitional kamma that has been done and accumulated.

Bhikkhus, among those, the three types of success in bodily action are wholesome volitional activity, resulting in happiness and yielding the fruit of happiness. The four types of success in verbal action are wholesome volitional activity, resulting in happiness and yielding the fruit of happiness. The three types of success in mental action are wholesome volitional activity, resulting in happiness and yielding the fruit of happiness.

Bhikkhus, how are the three types of success in bodily action wholesome volitional activity, resulting in happiness and yielding the fruit of happiness? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person abstains from the destruction of life,
500:
He has laid aside the rod, laid aside the weapon; he is conscientious and compassionate, dwelling with sympathy for the welfare of all living beings. ...

He abstains from taking what is not given. He does not take with the intent to steal the wealth and property of others, whether in the village or in the forest, that has not been given to him.

He gives up sexual misconduct and abstains from sexual misconduct. He does not have sexual relations with such women as are protected by their mother... or even those adorned with a garland of flowers. Thus, bhikkhus, the three types of success in bodily action are wholesome volitional activity, resulting in happiness and yielding the fruit of happiness.

Bhikkhus, how are the four types of success in verbal action wholesome volitional activity, resulting in happiness and yielding the fruit of happiness? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person gives up false speech and abstains from false speech. When he is in a council, or in an assembly, or among his relatives, or in a guild, or in the royal court, and is called as a witness and asked: 'Come, good man, tell what you know,' if he does not know, he says, 'I do not know'; if he knows, he says, 'I know'; if he has not seen, he says, 'I have not seen'; if he has seen, he says, 'I have seen.' Thus, he does not consciously tell a lie for his own sake, or for the sake of another, or for the sake of some material gain.

He gives up divisive speech and abstains from divisive speech. What he has heard here he does not repeat there to divide those people from these; what he has heard there he does not repeat here to divide these people from those. Thus he is a reconciler of those who are divided and a promoter of unity for those who are united. He loves concord, delights in concord, enjoys concord, and speaks words that create concord.

He gives up harsh speech and abstains from harsh speech. He speaks such words as are gentle, pleasing to the ear, lovely, reaching the heart, polite, desired by many, and agreeable to many.

He gives up idle chatter and abstains from idle chatter. He speaks at the right time, speaks what is true, speaks what is beneficial, speaks what is Dhamma, speaks what is Vinaya. At the right time, he speaks words that are worth recording, reasonable, moderate, and beneficial.
501:
Monks, in this way, the fourfold accomplishment of verbal action, having wholesome volition, results in happiness and has happiness as its fruit. Monks, how is the threefold accomplishment of mental action, having wholesome volition, productive of happiness and has happiness as its fruit? Here, monks, a certain person is not covetous. He does not covet the wealth and property of others, thinking, 'O, may what belongs to another be mine!'

He is one with a mind without ill will, with thoughts free from malice: 'May these beings be free from enmity, free from ill will, free from distress, and may they look after themselves happily.'

He has Right View and an undistorted vision: 'There is what is given, there is what is offered... there are in the world recluses and brahmins who, having realized for themselves by direct knowledge this world and the next, make them known, who have reached the upright Ariyan path and practice well.' Monks, in this way, the threefold accomplishment of mental action, having wholesome volition, results in happiness and has happiness as its fruit. Monks, it is because of the threefold accomplishment of bodily action which is wholesome volition that beings, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world. Monks, it is because of the fourfold accomplishment of verbal action which is wholesome volition that beings, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world. It is because of the threefold accomplishment of mental action which is wholesome volition that beings, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

Monks, just as a four-sided die thrown upwards, however it falls, it rests firmly; in the same way, monks, it is because of the threefold accomplishment of bodily action which is wholesome volition that beings, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.

It is because of the fourfold accomplishment of verbal action which is wholesome volition that beings, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world. It is because of the threefold accomplishment of mental action which is wholesome volition that beings, with the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world. Monks, I do not say that there is a wiping out of intentional kamma that has been done and accumulated without it being experienced. And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent life. Monks, I do not say that there is an ending of suffering without having experienced intentional kamma that has been done and accumulated." (The seventh discourse).
502:
The Seventh Discourse.

## 8. Dutiya Sañcetanika Sutta

218. Monks, I do not say that there is a wiping out of intentional kamma that has been done and accumulated without it being experienced. And that may be in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent life. Monks, I do not say that there is an ending of suffering without having experienced intentional kamma that has been done and accumulated.

Among those, monks, the threefold failure and corruption of bodily action, having unwholesome volition, results in suffering and has suffering as its fruit. The fourfold failure and corruption of verbal action, having unwholesome volition, results in suffering and has suffering as its fruit. The threefold failure and corruption of mental action, having unwholesome volition, results in suffering and has suffering as its fruit. Monks, I do not say that there is a wiping out of intentional kamma that has been done and accumulated without it being experienced. And that may be in this very life...
503:
...in the next life or in some subsequent existence. Monks, I do not say that there is an ending of suffering without having experienced the results of intentional actions that have been performed and accumulated.

Monks, among those actions, the threefold success of bodily action is of wholesome intention, bringing happiness and resulting in happiness. The fourfold success of verbal action is of wholesome intention, bringing happiness and resulting in happiness. The threefold success of mental action is of wholesome intention, bringing happiness and resulting in happiness.

And how, monks, is the threefold success of bodily action of wholesome intention, bringing happiness and resulting in happiness? ... (as before) ... Thus, monks, is the threefold success of bodily action of wholesome intention, bringing happiness and resulting in happiness.

And how, monks, is the fourfold success of verbal action of wholesome intention, bringing happiness and resulting in happiness? ... (as before) ... Thus, monks, is the fourfold success of verbal action of wholesome intention, bringing happiness and resulting in happiness.

And how, monks, is the threefold success of mental action of wholesome intention, bringing happiness and resulting in happiness? ... (as before) ... Thus, monks, is the threefold success of mental action of wholesome intention, bringing happiness and resulting in happiness.

Monks, because of the reason of the threefold success of bodily action which is wholesome intention, beings, after the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world. Because of the fourfold success of verbal action ... (as before) ... Because of the reason of the threefold success of mental action which is wholesome intention, beings, after the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world. ...

## 9. Karajakāya Sutta

219. Monks, I do not say that there is a wiping out of intentional actions that have been performed and accumulated without having experienced their results, whether in this very life, in the next life, or in some subsequent existence. Monks, I do not say that there is an ending of suffering without having experienced the results of intentional actions that have been performed and accumulated.

Monks, that noble disciple, thus free from covetousness, free from ill will, unconfused, clearly comprehending, and mindful, dwells pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness.
504:
Likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus, above, below, across, everywhere, and to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will.

He understands thus: 'Formerly, this mind of mine was limited and undeveloped, but now this mind of mine is immeasurable and well-developed. Whatever limited action (kamma of the sense sphere) was done, it does not remain there, it does not persist there.'

What do you think, monks? If this youth, from his childhood, were to develop the liberation of mind by loving-kindness, would he then perform any evil action? "No, venerable sir."

Not performing any evil action, would suffering touch him? "No, venerable sir. For, venerable sir, how could suffering touch one who performs no evil action?"

Monks, this liberation of mind by loving-kindness should be developed by a woman or a man. Monks, a woman or a man cannot take this body and go. Monks, this mortal being has consciousness as its condition. He understands thus: 'Whatever evil action I have formerly done with this physical body (karajakāya), all that is to be experienced here, and it will not follow me to a future existence.' Monks, the liberation of mind by loving-kindness thus developed leads to the state of a Non-returner, if the wise monk here does not penetrate a higher liberation (the fruit of Arahantship).

He dwells pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with compassion... with a mind imbued with appreciative joy... with a mind imbued with equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus, above, below, across, everywhere, and to all as to himself, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with equanimity—abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility, and without ill will.

He understands thus: 'Formerly, this mind of mine was limited and undeveloped, but now this mind of mine is immeasurable and well-developed. Whatever limited action was done, it does not remain there, it does not persist there.'
505:
“It does not remain in that (mahagguta kamma),” he knows thus. “Monks, what do you think? If this boy, from his youth, were to develop the liberation of mind through equanimity, would he do any evil deed?”
“No, Bhante.”
“For one who does no evil deed, would suffering touch him?”
“No, Bhante. Indeed, Bhante, for one who does no evil deed, from where would suffering come?”

“Monks, this liberation of mind through equanimity should be developed by a woman or a man. Monks, neither a woman nor a man can take this body and go. Monks, this mortal being is driven by the mind. He understands thus: ‘Whatever evil deed I have done before with this physical body, all that is to be felt here; it will not follow me [to a future state].’ Monks, the liberation of mind through equanimity, thus developed, leads to the state of a Non-returner for a wise monk here who has not yet penetrated a higher liberation (Arahantship).”

Ninth Sutta.

1. This refers to the fact that a being such as a human or a deva can only arise when the rebirth-linking consciousness occurs after the death-consciousness has fallen.

## 10. Adhammacariya Sutta

220. Then a certain Brahmin approached the Blessed One and, after exchanging friendly and courteous greetings, sat down to one side. Sitting there, that Brahmin said to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, what is the cause, what is the reason, why some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of misery, a bad destination, a state of ruin, in hell?”

“Brahmin, it is because of unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of misery, a bad destination, a state of ruin, in hell.”

“Master Gotama, what is the cause, what is the reason, why some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world?”

“Brahmin, it is because of righteous conduct and balanced conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.”

“I do not understand the meaning of Master Gotama’s brief statement in detail. It would be good if Master Gotama would teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might understand the meaning of Master Gotama’s brief statement in detail.”

“Then listen, Brahmin, pay close attention, I will speak.”
“Yes, Bhante,” the Brahmin replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Brahmin, unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct of the body is of three kinds;
506:
unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct of speech is of four kinds; unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct of the mind is of three kinds.

And how, Brahmin, is unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct of the body of three kinds? ... [Pe] ... Thus, Brahmin, unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct of the body is of three kinds.

And how, Brahmin, is unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct of speech of four kinds? ... [Pe] ... Thus, Brahmin, unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct of speech is of four kinds.

And how, Brahmin, is unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct of the mind of three kinds? ... [Pe] ... Thus, Brahmin, unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct of the mind is of three kinds. It is because of such unrighteous conduct and unbalanced conduct, Brahmin, that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of misery, a bad destination, a state of ruin, in hell.

Brahmin, righteous conduct and balanced conduct of the body is of three kinds; righteous conduct and balanced conduct of speech is of four kinds; righteous conduct and balanced conduct of the mind is of three kinds.

And how, Brahmin, is righteous conduct and balanced conduct of the body of three kinds? ... [Pe] ... Thus, Brahmin, righteous conduct and balanced conduct of the body is of three kinds.

And how, Brahmin, is righteous conduct and balanced conduct of speech of four kinds? ... [Pe] ... Thus, Brahmin, righteous conduct and balanced conduct of speech is of four kinds.

And how, Brahmin, is righteous conduct and balanced conduct of the mind of three kinds? ... [Pe] ... Thus, Brahmin, righteous conduct and balanced conduct of the mind is of three kinds. It is because of such righteous conduct and balanced conduct, Brahmin, that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.”

“Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama! ... [Pe] ... May Master Gotama accept me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.”

Tenth Sutta.

The First Chapter: The Chapter on the Physical Body (Karajakāya Vagga).
507:
The first, the Karajakāya Vagga, is finished.

## (22) 2. Sāmañña Vagga

221. Monks, possessed of ten qualities, one is deposited in hell as if brought and cast down there. What ten? One is a killer of living beings, one is a taker of what is not given, one is a wrongdoer in sensual pleasures, one is a speaker of falsehood, one is a speaker of divisive speech, one is a speaker of harsh speech, one is a speaker of idle chatter, one is covetous, one has a mind of ill will, and one holds wrong view. Monks, possessed of these ten qualities, one is deposited in hell as if brought and cast down there.

Monks, possessed of ten qualities, one is deposited in heaven as if brought and placed there. What ten? One abstains from killing living beings, one abstains from taking what is not given, one abstains from sexual misconduct, one abstains from speaking falsehood, one abstains from divisive speech, one abstains from harsh speech, one abstains from idle chatter, one is not covetous, one does not have a mind of ill will, and one holds right view.

Monks, possessed of these ten qualities, one is deposited in heaven as if brought and placed there. (1)

## 23. Rāgapeyyāla

237. "Monks, for the direct knowledge of lust (rāga), ten things should be developed. Which ten? The perception of foulness (asubhasaññā), the perception of death (maraṇasaññā), the perception of the repulsiveness in food (āhāre paṭikūlasaññā), the perception of non-delight in the entire world (sabbaloke anabhiratisaññā), the perception of impermanence (aniccasaññā), the perception of suffering in the impermanent (anicce dukkhasaññā), the perception of non-self in suffering (dukkhe anattasaññā), the perception of abandoning (pahānasaññā), the perception of dispassion (virāgasaññā), and the perception of cessation (niroredhasaññā). Monks, for the direct knowledge of lust, these ten things should be developed."
